source.title: Investigation 1 · Find an output
source.idea: Connect a starting balance and a per-turn change to an exact output.
teach: A fictional token account starts at -3 net tokens. Negative balances mean tokens owed, never a negative count of objects. Each turn adds 1/2 tokens. Inputs are whole turns from 0 to 6.

In y = (1/2) × x + (-3), x counts turns and y is the net balance. The rate m is 1/2; the start b is -3. At zero turns the balance equals the start. A two-turn change is 1 tokens, while the one-turn rate is 1/2.

items.prompt: Name this account’s rate and starting balance.
guidance: Read the value at x = 0 for the start.
Compare neighboring outputs for the per-turn change.
items.hint: The starting value and per-turn change answer different questions.
items.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.
items.explanation: The rate is 1/2 net tokens per turn and the start is -3 net tokens.

items.prompt: What is the net balance at 2 turns?
guidance: First multiply the rate 1/2 by 2.
Then add the signed starting balance -3.
items.hint: A negative start represents an amount owed. Add the per-turn changes to that signed value.
items.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.
items.explanation: y = (1/2) × x + (-3) at x = 2 gives 1 + (-3) = -2 net tokens.

items.prompt: Separate a total change from the starting value.
guidance: Two turns add two equal one-turn changes.
items.hint: The two-turn change is twice the rate; the start remains the value at zero turns.
items.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.
items.explanation: Two turns change the balance by 1; the start remains -3.

item.prompt: What is the net balance at 2 turns?
guidance: First multiply the rate 1/2 by 2.
Then add the signed starting balance -3.
item.hint: A negative start represents an amount owed. Add the per-turn changes to that signed value.
item.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.
item.explanation: y = (1/2) × x + (-3) at x = 2 gives 1 + (-3) = -2 net tokens.

checks.feedback: These values fit. y = (1/2) × x + (-3) at x = 2 gives 1 + (-3) = -2 net tokens.

item.prompt: What is the net balance at 2 turns?
guidance: First multiply the rate 1/2 by 2.

item.hint: A negative start represents an amount owed. Add the per-turn changes to that signed value.

item.explanation: y = (1/2) × x + (-3) at x = 2 gives 1 + (-3) = -2 net tokens.

source.title: Investigation 13 · Find an input
source.idea: Change the unknown: undo the start and the rate to find a number of turns.
teach: A fictional token account starts at -3 net tokens. Negative balances mean tokens owed, never a negative count of objects. Each turn adds 2 tokens. Inputs are whole turns from 0 to 6.

In y = (2) × x + (-3), x counts turns and y is the net balance. The rate m is 2; the start b is -3. At zero turns the balance equals the start. A two-turn change is 4 tokens, while the one-turn rate is 2.

To reach 1, solve (2)x + (-3) = 1. Subtract the signed start (-3) from BOTH sides: (2)x = 4. Divide BOTH sides by 2; then substitute the resulting input into the original rule. Subtracting a negative start adds its opposite.

items.prompt: Use the rule to find the balance at 2 turns.
guidance: Multiply 2 by 2, then add (-3).
items.hint: Keep change and starting balance separate.
items.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.
items.explanation: The output is 1 net tokens.

items.prompt: How many turns reach a net balance of 1?

fields.label: Right side after subtracting the signed start on BOTH sides

items.hint: Subtract (-3) from both sides before dividing both sides by the rate 2.
items.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.
items.explanation: After subtracting (-3), (2)x = 4; dividing gives x = 2. Substitution gives 1.

items.prompt: A different account changes by 4 net tokens over TWO turns. What is its one-turn rate?
guidance: A two-turn change combines two equal one-turn changes.
items.hint: Divide the total change by the number of turns.
items.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.
items.explanation: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 net tokens per turn.

item.prompt: How many turns reach a net balance of 1?

fields.label: Right side after subtracting the signed start on BOTH sides

item.hint: Subtract (-3) from both sides before dividing both sides by the rate 2.
item.example: Different model: y = (5/2) × x − 4. At x = 6 the balance is 15 − 4 = 11. To reach 11, add 4 to BOTH sides, giving (5/2)x = 15; divide BOTH sides by 5/2 to get x = 6. Substitute to check.

source.title: Investigation 48 · Compare two rules
source.idea: Two rates and two starts determine where balances meet and which is greater.
teach: A fictional token account starts at 0 net tokens. Negative balances mean tokens owed, never a negative count of objects. Each turn adds 5/2 tokens. Inputs are whole turns from 0 to 6.

In y = (5/2) × x + (0), x counts turns and y is the net balance. The rate m is 5/2; the start b is 0. At zero turns the balance equals the start. A two-turn change is 5 tokens, while the one-turn rate is 5/2.
Account B starts at 2 and adds 2 each turn. Its rule is y = (2) × x + (2). B starts 2 above A, while A gains 1/2 more per turn.

Set the two expressions equal. Subtract B’s rate × x and A’s signed start from BOTH sides to obtain (1/2)x = 2. Divide both sides by 1/2 and substitute in both original rules. Which balance is greater can change at the meeting input; a higher rate alone does not determine the larger output.

items.prompt: Name the two differences between the accounts.
guidance: Subtract the signed starting values.
Subtract the rates using equal units.
items.hint: The starting gap closes by the difference in rates each turn.
items.example: Different pair: A = 2x − 4; B = x + 1. Set equal: 2x − 4 = x + 1. Subtract x and add 4 on BOTH sides: x = 5, both balances 6. At x = 4, A = 4 and B = 5; at x = 6, A = 8 and B = 7.
items.explanation: B starts 2 above A; A gains 1/2 more per turn.

items.prompt: At what input do the two balances meet?
items.hint: Set the two original expressions equal. Do the same operation to BOTH sides, then substitute into BOTH rules.
items.example: Different pair: A = 2x − 4; B = x + 1. Set equal: 2x − 4 = x + 1. Subtract x and add 4 on BOTH sides: x = 5, both balances 6. At x = 4, A = 4 and B = 5; at x = 6, A = 8 and B = 7.
items.explanation: (1/2)x = 2, so x = 4. Both balances are 10.

items.prompt: Compare on each side of the meeting: find both balances at 3 and 5 turns.
guidance: Use each account’s own start and rate.
Compare the two outputs at the SAME input.
items.hint: A lower balance can mean more debt. Do not choose by slope alone.
items.example: Different pair: A = 2x − 4; B = x + 1. Set equal: 2x − 4 = x + 1. Subtract x and add 4 on BOTH sides: x = 5, both balances 6. At x = 4, A = 4 and B = 5; at x = 6, A = 8 and B = 7.
items.explanation: Before the meeting A = 15/2, B = 8, so B is greater. After it A = 25/2, B = 12, so A is greater.

item.prompt: At what input do the two balances meet?
item.hint: Set the two original expressions equal. Do the same operation to BOTH sides, then substitute into BOTH rules.
item.example: Different pair: A = 2x − 4; B = x + 1. Set equal: 2x − 4 = x + 1. Subtract x and add 4 on BOTH sides: x = 5, both balances 6. At x = 4, A = 4 and B = 5; at x = 6, A = 8 and B = 7.

checks.feedback: These values fit. (1/2)x = 2, so x = 4. Both balances are 10.

source.title: Investigation 48 · Compare two rules
source.idea: Two rates and two starts determine where balances meet and which is greater.
teach: A fictional token account starts at 0 net tokens. Negative balances mean tokens owed, never a negative count of objects. Each turn adds 5/2 tokens. Inputs are whole turns from 0 to 6.

In y = (5/2) × x + (0), x counts turns and y is the net balance. The rate m is 5/2; the start b is 0. At zero turns the balance equals the start. A two-turn change is 5 tokens, while the one-turn rate is 5/2.
Account B starts at 2 and adds 2 each turn. Its rule is y = (2) × x + (2). B starts 2 above A, while A gains 1/2 more per turn.

Set the two expressions equal. Subtract B’s rate × x and A’s signed start from BOTH sides to obtain (1/2)x = 2. Divide both sides by 1/2 and substitute in both original rules. Which balance is greater can change at the meeting input; a higher rate alone does not determine the larger output.

items.prompt: Name the two differences between the accounts.
guidance: Subtract the signed starting values.
Subtract the rates using equal units.
items.hint: The starting gap closes by the difference in rates each turn.
items.example: Different pair: A = 2x − 4; B = x + 1. Set equal: 2x − 4 = x + 1. Subtract x and add 4 on BOTH sides: x = 5, both balances 6. At x = 4, A = 4 and B = 5; at x = 6, A = 8 and B = 7.
items.explanation: B starts 2 above A; A gains 1/2 more per turn.
